newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says strikes deal with U.S. on Helms-Burton.
newsitem.headline: EU says strikes deal with U.S. on Helms-Burton.

text.p: The European Commission said Friday it struck a deal with the United States settling their trade dispute over the Helms-Burton anti-Cuba legislation.

The Helms-Burton Act, which aims to isolate the government of Fidel Castro, seeks to stop investment in property in Cuba deemed by Washington to have been stolen from U.S. citizens. Among other things, it allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreign companies that have investments in property confiscated by Havana since the communist revolution of 1959.

European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said in a statement that the deal would "chart a path toward a longer-term solution through amendment of the Helms Burton Act." It would also allow for talks with the EU over the question of extraterritorial application of trade laws.
"In particular, the agreement will enable us to address with the U.S. and resolve the problems caused by legislation that inhibits investment in third countries," he said.
